title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the page, since the definitions of M, M_N and τ_N are on earlier pages): S is a graded ring and M is a category of graded S-modules. The page's notation for S is written 'S^k_k'; whether S is bigraded is unclear. The constraints on the page fix the reading. First, τ_N P ⊂ P is a submodule. Second, any degree-i map τ_{N-i}S → P lands in τ_N P. Third, q_N kills the submodule generated by the P_i with i<N. Together these suggest:
- τ_n(-) is the truncation 'degrees ≥ n', so τ_{N-i}S = S_{≥N-i}, an ideal of S.
- M_N is the full subcategory of modules concentrated in degrees ≥ N.
- i_N : M_N → M is the inclusion.

b) Grothendieck defines φ_N : M_N → M by (φ_N Q)_i = Hom^i_M(τ_{N-i}S, Q) = Hom^0_M(τ_{N-i}S[-i], Q). The module structure comes from transposing the multiplications u : τ_{N-i-k}S → τ_{N-i}S (degree k, for u of degree k). Restriction along τ_{N-i}S ⊂ S gives a map to Hom^i(S,Q) = Q_i. This yields a natural map φ_N(Q) → i_N(Q) (10.2.1). Applying τ_N gives τ_N φ_N Q ≅ Q (10.2.2), because for i ≥ N one has τ_{N-i}S = S. This is the counit of an adjunction.

The unit P → φ_N τ_N P (10.2.3) is P_i ≅ Hom^i(S,P) → Hom^i(τ_{N-i}S, P) = Hom^i(τ_{N-i}S, τ_N P). The last equality holds because a degree-i map defined on S_{≥N-i} lands in P_{≥N}. Hence τ_N ⊣ φ_N.

c) Grothendieck adds 'for conscience' the left adjoint of i_N: q_N(P) = P / (submodule generated by the P_i, i < N). He notes it will not be used.

The result is an adjoint string q_N ⊣ i_N ⊣ τ_N ⊣ φ_N relating graded modules to modules 'truncated below'. Here φ_N is a degree-wise ideal-transform / coinduction functor of the form Hom(S_{≥n}, -), familiar from the description of sections over Proj. This is a technical lemma, apparently in preparation for a truncation/filtration argument for divided-power de Rham complexes. The neighbouring pages (an ℓ-adic monodromy text and an analysis exercise sheet) are unrelated archive material.
errors: No mathematical error detected, given the inferred definitions. The verification that the unit map is well defined (S_{≥N-i} times degree i lands in degrees ≥ N) is stated rather than proved, but it is immediate.
The identification of τ_N as 'degrees ≥ N' is inferred; the page does not define it.

ideas.what: Right adjoint φ_N of the truncation τ_N, given by (φ_N Q)_i = Hom^i(S_{≥N-i}, Q), with counit τ_N φ_N ≅ id
ideas.modern_name: Coinduction / ideal-transform-type right adjoint; recollement-style adjoint string for truncation of graded modules
